abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions are designed around the app's actual variation and mostly stretch well (an Items page would reuse nearly everything); the home-page card duplication and the ID-keyed SpeciesIndex are the seams that would force copying under the next similar-but-different requirement.

findings.issue: Home builds Pokémon cards inline (id/name/sprite/types) instead of going through cardsFromPokemon, duplicating card construction in a second place.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared species-index card builder in lib/api.server.ts (or let cardsFromPokemon accept pre-resolved ids) so all four card lists share one construction path.

findings.issue: SpeciesIndex is Map<number,string> keyed by a single 'id' that is used both as species ID (home.tsx:41,62) and Pokémon ID (cardsFromPokemon, api.server.ts:247-249), conflating two identities that the spec warns can differ (deoxys vs deoxys-normal).
findings.suggestion: Key the index by Pokémon name (or carry {speciesName, pokemonId} per entry) so sprite ID and species name can diverge without redesigning the index.

findings.issue: The alternate-form exclusion rule is duplicated as two magic literals (id <= 10000 here, id > 10000 at api.server.ts:249).
findings.suggestion: Export a named constant (e.g. MAX_SPECIES_ID) or a shared isAlternateForm(id) helper from lib/api.server.ts and use it in both places.

findings.issue: The 'Not found – Pokédex' meta fallback is repeated verbatim in four route modules (also move.tsx:15, ability.tsx:14, type.tsx:17), plus root.tsx computes its own error heading.
findings.suggestion: Add a shared metaFor(heading | 'not-found') helper in lib/format.ts (or a small route-helper module) and use it from all metas.

findings.issue: The type-label fallback `typeNames[name] ?? humanize(name)` is re-implemented in pokemon.tsx:47, type.tsx:23, move.tsx:23 and home.tsx:66, and home builds its own label map at home.tsx:31.
findings.suggestion: Move label lookup into lib/api.server.ts next to getTypeNames (e.g. a typeLabel(name, typeNames) helper) so one place owns the fallback rule.

findings.issue: Card.hidden and its 'Hidden ability' rendering are ability-specific concerns baked into the generic Card type and card component; removing abilities leaves dead presentation code.
findings.suggestion: Either accept it as a generic card annotation or render the hidden-ability note from the ability route via a slot/child prop instead of a Card field.

findings.issue: MoveTables sort-state reset relies on the implicit key={p.game} remount; a future refactor of MoveTables props could silently break the reset.
findings.suggestion: Keep it but add a short comment stating the key intentionally resets sort state on game change.

summary: A tidy, idiomatic React Router v8 codebase where loaders, an API module and shared UI components form clean seams, so infrastructure changes (base URL, caching, sprite URL, formatting) are one-file edits. The main editability cost is the Pokémon-card domain: home builds cards inline while the other three lists use cardsFromPokemon, and SpeciesIndex conflates Pokémon and species IDs, so the likeliest data bug is a two-file fix rather than a one-liner. Everything else — adding an Items page, sorting, removing a route — is straightforward because the abstractions are small and reused rather than copied.
